LESSON: MULTIPLICATION (8

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.4: Multiplication (8

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Multiplication (8. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: When can you use multiplication in real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. multiply up to a two-digit number by multiples of in different situations
2. multiply up to a two-digit number by two-digit number with and without regrouping
3. multiply up to a two digit number by in different situations
4. estimate products by rounding off numbers to the nearest with product not exceeding 1,, e)

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Multiplication (8.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Multiplication (8 using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Team up with peers to multiply two-digit numbers by multiples of 10 using number cards or charts,
2. Team up with others to multiply up to a two-digit number by two- digit number with and without regrouping using counters and prepare a corresponding multiplication chart,
3. Share tasks while generating patterns involving multiplication with products not exceeding 100 and prepare multiplication charts using locally available materials,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When can you use multiplication in real life?
2. How can you create patterns involving multiplication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Multiplication (8 is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
